note: TIRING AND IDLE (Dave 21 Nov 2026): 'scale in between 50 fitness being 100% and 100 being 50%': from fitness 50 up the exertion rise falls in a straight line from 100 percent to top_mult (50 percent) at 100, so 75 is 75 percent and a fitness 100 character runs twice as long as an average one before winded; under 50 the exp(-(fitness-50)/5 x strength) curve below is kept (0 is about 165 percent, 40 about 110 percent; it meets the line at 50 with the same slope). 'being Idle can lower it below your start. that was not my rule. remove it.': true rest now takes points off below the creation value too, down to min (0); the rest of the training rules are unchanged, and training still adds at most max_gain above the creation value. Older text below that says otherwise is history. START (Dave 19 Nov 2026: 'fitness should just start rolled in the middle range', for player characters): a new player character's fitness is rolled 40 to 60 (attributes.json player_bands), replacing the fixed start of 5 below (FIT-1); default (50, average) is only for a character with no fitness saved and for tools and tests. SCALE (Dave 19 Nov 2026, data/items/attributes.json): fitness is now 0 to 100 like every attribute, 50 an average adult; each 5 points does what one point did on the old -10 to +10 scale described below (strength is per 5 points, the rise is multiplied by exp(-(fitness-50)/5 x strength)), so 75 is the old 5 and the training numbers are scaled to keep the same pace: xp_per_point 200 (5 points take the old 1000 XP), max_gain 50, decay_s_per_point 8640 (5 points per the old 12 h). Older saves are converted at load. The old-scale text follows. Fitness (Dave 2026-10-21): a character attribute, a whole number min to max (-10 to +10), 0 an average adult, that directly sets how fast exertion rises during strenuous activity (running, climbing, tool work, heavy loads): the rise per second is multiplied by exp(-fitness x strength), so +10 fitness at strength 0.05 raises exertion at about 61 percent of the normal pace (winded after about 1.65 times as long) and -10 at about 165 percent. Falling (recovery) is not touched. It is stored with the character in characters.json like luck. New characters start at default: 5 (Dave 18 Nov 2026: 'characters should not start out feeble', a fit 20 year old; provisional FIT-1, was 0), so exertion rises at about 78 percent of an average adult's pace and 5 points are left to train. Characters saved before this keep their saved value. Training (Dave 2026-10-21: starts fixed, trains slowly): the creation value is the base; any physical effort trains it like a skill (Dave 2 Nov 2026): effort above min_effort (0.1) earns XP every tick_s (10 s) tick into the day's bucket (xp_today, saved with the character), paid out as points at game midnight, or at the next tick after login if midnight passed while away: xp_base (1) + xp_per_effort (2) x effort, so 1 at the line, 1.8 at a steady walk (effort 0.4, was 0.5 before BUGLIST-001 BUG-005) and 3 at a run, up to max_effort; xp_per_point (1000) XP make one point at every level, up to max_gain above the base (Dave 4 Nov, BUG-023). Walking alone is about 15 hours (14 before BUGLIST-001 BUG-005 lowered the walking effort to 0.4) from 0 to +10, running about 9. Effort between rest_effort (0.02) and min_effort neither earns nor costs. Only effort under rest_effort for more than rest_grace_s loses one point per decay_s_per_point (12 h), never below the base (replaced 21 Nov 2026, see the top); sleep is neutral (Sonny 4 Nov: a night in bed is recovery, not idleness). Today's training shows on the Tab screen (protocol 92). set_fitness() sets the base and clears the training. Set strength to 0 to switch fitness off.
